project.name: Project Alpha — Response-Speed Training
project.description: A personal training program for faster, clearer decisions across executive communication, a precision skill domain, and general reaction time. The program has three layers: hardware, domain-specific software, and pressure plus feedback.

documents.title: Training Program — Full Synthesis & Weekly Template
documents.content: The program treats processing speed as a compressed perception-to-decision-to-action loop built through chunking and automaticity. Its three layers are Hardware (sleep, aerobic capacity, regulation, physical consistency), Software (domain-specific practice such as pitch dry fire and precision-skill reps), and Pressure + Feedback (timers, stress exposure, and after-action reviews). The week-one launch list is: begin the noon caffeine cutoff, complete daily core stability, run the first hostile-pitch session, enroll in improv, obtain the documented supplements, and log a PVT baseline.

documents.title: Caffeine & Supplement Protocol
documents.content: The current high daily caffeine dose is likely maintaining tolerance while later intake reduces sleep quality. The protocol is: first dose 60–90 minutes after waking, a hard cutoff at noon, and no more than 300 mg total per day. Creatine and L-theanine are optional supporting interventions; the document explicitly treats sleep consistency and caffeine timing as higher-leverage than supplements.

documents.title: Measurement & Telemetry Protocol
documents.content: The weekly Sunday review logs PVT median reaction time, pitch time-to-first-word, filler count, sprint time, fixed practice par time, resting heart rate or HRV when available, sleep, and an in-sync score. The in-sync score is a subjective 1–10 rating of how coordinated and mentally sharp the operator felt. It is not a clinical measure; its value is in tracking correlations with the objective metrics under consistent conditions. A baseline should be captured before the caffeine reset.

documents.title: Research Notes — What Works and What Doesn't
documents.content: Commercial brain-training games can improve performance on their own games but have weak evidence for transfer to unrelated real-world skills. Dual n-back and generic sports-vision training have similar transfer limitations. A psychomotor vigilance task is retained as a measurement tool, not a broad training claim. The program favors aerobic work, sleep consistency, domain-specific deliberate practice, timers, and feedback loops.

documents.title: Project Alpha — Program Context
documents.content: State: active. Stage: execution. Snapshot status: eight open tasks and two overdue tasks. Next step: ship the training equipment to the specialist workshop for setup. The equipment setup is the hard gate for live precision-skill practice. Knowledge preparation can continue before setup. The program's operating rules are: protect consistency, time and review meaningful practice, train each target domain directly, and treat external task capture as a way to reduce working-memory load.

goals.name: Improve measurable response speed across communication, precision skills, and reaction time
goals.description: Success is a visible trend in PVT reaction time, pitch time-to-first-word, fixed practice times, and the in-sync score, plus qualitative improvement under pressure without sacrificing physical consistency.

plans.name: Hardware — sleep, caffeine, aerobic base, and physical consistency
plans.description: Protect the substrate with a fixed wake time, noon caffeine cutoff, daily core stability, gradual strength work, aerobic work, and a daily downregulation block.

plans.name: Software — domain practice and automaticity
plans.description: Build separate pattern libraries through hostile-pitch practice, precision-skill preparation, improv, and bounded deliberate gaming.

plans.name: Pressure & Feedback — measurement, stress exposure, and reviews
plans.description: Track PVT, pitch, physical, and subjective metrics; use one meaningful high-consequence practice event per week; and review correlations monthly.
